# Isaiah Chapter 32 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 152r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_032_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice. **2** Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry place, like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.

**3** Then the eyes of those who see will not be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen. **4** The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will speak clearly and fluently. **5** The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel said to be honorable. **6** For the fool speaks folly, and his heart plots iniquity — to practice ungodliness and to speak error concerning the LORD, to leave the hungry unsatisfied and to deprive the thirsty of drink. **7** As for the scoundrel, his schemes are evil; he devises wicked plans to ruin the afflicted with lying words, even when the plea of the needy is just. **8** But the noble one devises noble things, and by noble things he stands.

**9** Rise up, you women who are at ease; hear my voice! You complacent daughters, give ear to my speech! **10** In little more than a year you will tremble, you complacent ones, for the grape harvest will fail and the gathering will not come. **11** Tremble, you women who are at ease; shudder, you complacent ones! Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth on your waists. **12** Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine, **13** for the soil of my people, growing up in thorns and briers — indeed, for all the joyful houses in the jubilant city. **14** For the palace will be forsaken, the populous city deserted; hill and watchtower will become barren wastes forever, a delight of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks —

**15** until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is regarded as a forest. **16** Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will abide in the fruitful field. **17** The effect of righteousness will be peace, and the result of righteousness, quietness and trust forever. **18** My people will dwell in a peaceful habitation, in secure dwellings, and in undisturbed resting places. **19** It will hail when the forest comes down, and the city will be utterly laid low. **20** Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who let the feet of the ox and the donkey range free.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Isaiah 32 — "A King Will Reign in Righteousness" — part of First Isaiah (chs.1-39). The Assyrian crisis provides the historical backdrop.

---
## Disagreement Log

Minor register disagreements resolved through standard SOPHIA consensus process.
